newsitem.title: USA: Former AK chairman says steel prices to rise.
newsitem.headline: Former AK chairman says steel prices to rise.

text.p: Countering predictions from industry officials that steel prices will fall this year, the former chairman of AK Steel Holding Corp said Wednesday U.S. steelmakers will likely succeed at raising prices in May, following an already successful increase earlier this year.

"I think the chances (for prices rising in May) are good," said Thomas C. Graham, who officially retired from AK Steel in January but has been retained by the company as a consultant. "It's an appropriate time to raise prices."
Graham made his comments to reporters prior to a speaking engagement at Carnegie Mellon University's Graduate School of Industrial Administration.
Major U.S. steelmakers last week said they would raise prices by about three percent in May. The industry already pushed through a three percent hike to its customers that took effect in January.

Some industry analysts and steel buyers scoffed recently at the May announcement, predicting that prices will instead fall as new domestic capacity enters the market this year, primarily from upstart minimill producers.
Graham, however, said the May increase will likely succeed because steel demand is strong and steelmakers are pushing production limits to meet that demand.
"(Despite) the capacity increases, the industry has been challenged to fill the requirements of the market," he said.
Graham, 70, said his consultant agreement with AK Steel runs on a year-to-year basis and he currently had no plans to work full time at another steel company.

At the time of Graham's retirement, many industry officials had speculated that he would go on to head another steel firm. Graham has worked in the steel industry since 1947 and has gained a reputation for taking the helm at financially troubled steelmakers and making them profitable.
Two companies in particular that had been cited as possibilities for Graham were Armco Inc and Bethlehem Steel Corp, both of which have been plagued with unprofitable operations.
